text: Dollywood is a theme park jointly owned by Herschend and Dolly Parton through her entertainment company, Dolly Parton Productions, and is located in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, within the Knoxville metropolitan area near the gateway to The Great Smoky Mountains. It hosts nearly 3 million guests annually from mid-March to the Christmas holidays and is the largest ticketed tourist attraction in Tennessee, having won several international awards. In addition to thrill rides, the park features traditional Smoky Mountain crafts, food, and music, hosting concerts and musical events each year, including performances by Dolly Parton and her family as well as national and local acts. The park is part of a 150-acre (61 ha) Dollywood amusement destination that includes the 35-acre (14 ha) Dollywood's Splash Country water park, the 20-acre (8.1 ha) Dollywood's DreamMore Resort and Spa, and the 5-acre (2.0 ha) Dolly Parton's Stampede Dinner Attraction. Originally opened on June 10, 1961, as "Rebel Railroad" by the Robbins brothers from Blowing Rock, North Carolina, the park was themed around the centennial of the Civil War, featuring a steam train, general store, blacksmith shop, and saloon, with riders protected by Confederates from attacks by Union soldiers, train robbers, and Native Americans. It was modeled after their earlier park, Tweetsie Railroad. In 1964, it was renamed "Goldrush Junction" with a wild west theme similar to Tweetsie Railroad. In 1970, Art Modell, owner of the Cleveland Browns, purchased the park and added an outdoor theater and the Robert F. Thomas Chapel. In 1975, the name changed to "Goldrush," and in 1976, Jack and Pete Herschend, owners of Silver Dollar City, bought the park, which continued operating as Goldrush that year. In 1977, the Herschends renamed it "Silver Dollar City Tennessee" to make it a sister park to their original Silver Dollar City in Branson, Missouri, spending about $1 million on upgrades and adding two new steam locomotives, #70 and #71, and the remains of engine #72 from the White Pass & Yukon Route Railroad. In 1986, Dolly Parton, who grew up in the area, acquired an interest in the park and it reopened on May 3, 1986, as "Dollywood." Parton stated she became involved to bring jobs to her home region after achieving success in her career. The park employs approximately 4,000 people, making it the largest employer in the community. From 1986 to 2010, the park doubled in size to 150 acres (61 ha). On November 16, 2010, Dollywood earned the Liseberg Applause Award, which Dolly Parton accepted at the IAAPA Attractions Expo 2010 in Orlando. The 1986 reopening included the Rivertown Junction area with Smoky Mountain River Rampage, Back Porch Theater, Aunt Granny's Dixie Fixins' Restaurant, Dolly's Tennessee Mountain Home, and "Rags to Riches: The Dolly Parton Story" museum; the "The Butter Churn" ride was removed, and attendance doubled to over a million guests. In 1987, the Daydream Ridge area opened with the Mountain Slidewinder, Mountain Dan's Burger House, Sweet Dreams Candy Shop, The Rainbow Factory, and Critter Creek Playground; engine #70 was restored. In 1988, the 1,739-seat Celebrity Theater opened with the "Showcase of Stars" concert series. Five new children's rides were added to Fun Country, including a Zamperla Balloon Race. The Dollywood Foundation was established to provide books and school supplies to children in Sevier County. In 1989, Thunder Express, a steel mine train coaster, was built adjacent to Blazing Fury and relocated from Six Flags Over Mid-America; the 1989 season was the last for the National Mountain Music Festival. In 1990, a 1924 Dentzel Carousel was relocated to near the train depot, replacing the Silver Dollar Saloon; a 600-seat Gaslight Theater opened nearby. The Smoky Mountain Christmas Festival premiered in November, extending the operating season into December. In 1991, Eagle Mountain Sanctuary, an outdoor aviary, and the Wings of America Theater with the Birds of Prey show and the 300-seat Valley Theater were added. In 1992, the Showstreet area opened with the Showstreet Palace Theater, The Butterfly Emporium, The Backstage Restaurant, The Spotlight Bakery, Friendship Gardens, and WDLY-FM, a working radio station; the main entrance moved from Rivertown Junction to Showstreet; the Barnwood Theater became Imagination Station. Attendance topped 2 million for the first time in 1992. In 1993, Fun Country was renovated into The Country Fair with the Wonder Wheel (60 ft tall), Twist and Shout, and Tennessee Twister; the Balloon Race ride was relocated to Daydream Ridge. "Sunset Musicfest" debuted in 1994; the Gaslight Theater became the Heartsong Theater. In 1995, the Jukebox Junction 1950s "Main Street" area opened with Rockin' Roadway, The Pines Theater, Red's Diner, and Cas Walker's Music Store; Sunset Musicfest did not return. In 1996, the Dollywood Boulevard area opened with Thunder Road, Silver Screen Café, and Centerstage gift shop. In 1997, "U Pick Nick" aired in the Celebrity Theater; the Flooded Mine dark ride was closed and demolished in October; Silver Screen Café became DJ Platters. In 1998, Daredevil Falls, billed as "The Highest and Fastest Waterfall Ride in America" with a 62 ft (19 m) drop, opened in the former Flooded Mine location. Thunder Express was closed in September and sold to Magic Springs Theme Park in Arkansas; the antique carousel was removed and replaced with a new Chance Rides carousel. In 1999, the Tennessee Tornado steel looping coaster opened in the former Thunder Express area; the Southern Gospel Museum and Hall of Fame opened; the Balloon Race ride was removed. In 2000, Daydream Ridge was renovated into Dreamland Forest, a children's mountain-themed interactive play area. The Festival of Nations premiered in April 2001. In 2001, Dolly's Splash Country, a 25-acre (100,000 m²) water park, opened adjacent to Dollywood's parking lot. In 2002, Dollywood Boulevard was redeveloped into Adventures in Imagination; Smoky Mountain Wilderness Adventure replaced Thunder Road; a new Dolly museum, Chasing Rainbows, opened in the former DJ Platters building. In 2003, KidsFest premiered and Imagination Station became Celebration Hall; the "Showcase of Stars" concert series ended. In 2004, Thunderhead Gap opened with the Thunderhead wooden roller coaster; the Country Fair Falls log flume was demolished in November; most Country Fair rides, including the Swingamajig, Tennessee Twister, The Convoy, and The Barnstormer, were removed to make room for new rides in 2005, which included Dizzy Disk, Amazing Flying Elephants, Lemon Twist, Shooting Star, Sky Rider, VeggieTales Sideshow Spin, Waltzing Swinger, Piggy Parade, Busy Bees, and Lucky Ducky; the National Southern Gospel & Harvest Celebration debuted. In 2006, the Timber Tower ride, along with Lil' Loggers Landing, Beaver Creek, Beaver Creek Boat Float, and Lumberjack Lifts, opened in a new area adjacent to Thunderhead; the Barbeque & Bluegrass festival premiered. In 2007, Mystery Mine, a Gerstlauer Eurofighter coaster with two vertical lift hills, dark ride elements, fire effects, a 95-degree 85-foot (26 m) drop, a heartline roll, and a dive loop, opened using an abandoned mine shaft theme; the ride cost $17 million ($25.8 million in 2024 dollars). In 2008, River Battle, an interactive water raft ride, opened in Wilderness Pass, connecting Timber Canyon and Craftsman's Valley; "Thunder Road" returned to Imagination Cinema; Della's Lye Soap shop moved to Wilderness Pass; a new exhibit for the Wings of America show birds was relocated; the Polar Express 4-D Experience was shown during Smoky Mountain Christmas. In 2009, new shows "Imaginé" by Le Grand Cirque and "Sha-Kon-O-Hey! Land of Blue Smoke," featuring music by Dolly Parton and the story of the last family in the Smoky Mountains, were introduced; "Imaginé" headlined Festival of Nations; "Thunder Road" was renamed "White Lightning" and then replaced by Journey to the Center of the Earth: 4-D Adventure; a multi-line zipline attraction, SkyZip (owned by Skyline Eco-Adventures of Maui, Hawaii), opened as the first multi-line zip line tour in a theme park. In 2010, Adventure Mountain opened in Wilderness Pass at a cost of $5 million, featuring three adventure courses—Geyser Gorge, Black Bear Cliff, and Rocky Top—with 100 rope features, swinging beams, suspension bridges, flying islands, and floating stairs, ranging from a few inches to over 26 feet (7.9 m) in height; it included a scaled-down play area, Camp Teachittoomee; the park also brought back "Sha-Kon-O-Hey! Land of Blue Smoke" and changed its logo for its 25th anniversary. In 2011, Owens Farm with a $5.5 million giant swing, Barnstormer, replaced Dreamland Forest; the area included a play area for younger guests; Christmas on Ice, a new ice skating show, premiered in DP's Celebrity Theater and headlined Smoky Mountain Christmas. Wild Eagle opened on March 24, 2012, as the first Bolliger & Mabillard Wing Coaster in the United States and was the biggest investment in Dollywood history; in 2012, the operator of SkyZip sued Dollywood, blaming it for damaging the zip line network during construction of Wild Eagle, though Dollywood blamed storms; the two settled out of court, and Dollywood took over SkyZip operations, closing it in 2019; Timber Tower was dismantled before opening in 2012 due to a lawsuit with the manufacturer; the VeggieTales name was removed from Sideshow Spin in 2012; Adventure Mountain was permanently closed after the 2012 season. In 2013, Dollywood focused on family time, introducing Cirque Shanghai, Mystic India, One World Party, over 50 new international food items, "Great American Summer" (replacing KidsFest), including the Great American Country Show, Gazillion Bubbles, The Little Engine Playhouse, and Salute to America, extended hours, and a nightly fireworks show; Smoky Mountain Christmas added a show based on Dolly Parton's version of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol; the slogan was "Make Time for Happy!" and Imagination Cinema became Dreamsong Theater, playing Dolly's My People. In 2014, FireChaser Express, a dual-launch family coaster, replaced Adventure Mountain in Wilderness Pass; the slogan changed to "Love Every Moment"; Smoky Mountain Christmas added a Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer meet-and-greet, Holly Jolly Junction. Dollywood's DreamMore Resort and Spa opened adjacent to Dollywood's Splash Country in 2015. For its 30th anniversary, the park redesigned the resort entrance and added two new Festival of Nations shows, "Rhythm of the Dance" and "Timber"; Cas Walker's was demolished; six new shows were added to "Great American Summer"; the Showcase of Stars concert series was revived; Rock the Smokies, a Christian music festival, debuted; Rudolph and friends returned to Smoky Mountain Christmas. In 2010, Parton expressed interest in expanding Dollywood with new parks and a resort, stating they may eventually open in other parts of the country to reflect local culture. On August 21, 2013, Parton announced Dollywood's DreamMore Resort and Spa, which opened on July 27, 2015. On June 13, 2016, Lightning Rod, a Rocky Mountain Construction wooden coaster, opened as the world's first launched wooden coaster and the fastest wooden coaster in the world. In 2017, a 200-foot (61 m) freefall ride, Drop Line, opened to replace Timber Tower, along with a junior roller coaster, Whistle Punk Chaser; two new seasonal events debuted; Dollywood's Splash Country added the TailSpin Racer mat racer slide complex; Sideshow Spin and River Battle were removed. In 2018, the former River Battle site became the Plaza at Wilderness Pass, a covered open space for relaxation and seasonal events; the Spring Mix music series and the 2018 "Season of Showstoppers" marked the park's largest investment in entertainment; the Festival of Nations featured three new headliners: Flamenco Kings starring Los Vivancos (Pines Theater), National Dance Company of Siberia (Celebrity Theater), and Ladysmith Black Mambazo (Showstreet Palace Theater); the first Summer Celebration included DRUMLine Live! in Celebrity Theater.

Dollywood is organized into 11 themed areas—Showstreet, Rivertown Junction, Craftsman's Valley, The Village, Country Fair, Timber Canyon, Wilderness Pass, Jukebox Junction, Owens Farm, Adventures in Imagination, and Wildwood Grove—reflecting the historical eras and culture of East Tennessee, with Owens Farm and Adventures in Imagination exploring Dolly Parton's life and imagination. Many attractions focus on the history and culture of the Southern Appalachian region. The park features a variety of attractions, including Showstreet Palace Theater and Celebrity Theater, Dolly's Tennessee Mountain Home, Back Porch Theater, Smoky Mountain River Rampage, Dollywood Grist Mill, Valley Theater, Eagle Mountain Sanctuary, Wings of America Theater, Robert F. Thomas Chapel, Calico Falls Schoolhouse, Tennessee Tornado, Blazing Fury, Daredevil Falls, craft exhibits, the 3 ft (914 mm) narrow gauge Dollywood Express steam train, Imagination Playhouse, Village Carousel, The Amazing Flying Elephants, Lemon Twist, Shooting Star, Sky Rider, The Waltzing Swinger, Piggy Parade, Busy Bees, Lucky Ducky, Dolly's Demolition Derby, The Scrambler, Mystery Mine, Thunderhead, Drop Line, Whistle Punk Chaser, Lumberjack Lifts, Rockin' Roadway, Pines Theater, Lightning Rod, Barnstormer, Behind the Seams and Song-teller Museums, The Plaza at Wilderness Pass, Wild Eagle—America's first winged coaster—and FireChaser Express, a dual-launch coaster. In 2017, a 200-foot (61 m) freefall ride called Drop Line, which replaced Timber Tower, opened along with a junior roller coaster called Whistle Punk Chaser. Two new seasonal events debuted, and Dollywood's Splash Country added the TailSpin Racer mat racer slide complex. Sideshow Spin and River Battle were removed. In 2018, the former River Battle site was transformed into the Plaza at Wilderness Pass, a new open space with covered seating for relaxing and enjoying seasonal events. The 2018 "Season of Showstoppers" marked the park's largest investment in entertainment in its history, featuring headliners including Flamenco Kings starring Los Vivancos (Pines Theater), National Dance Company of Siberia (Celebrity Theater), and Ladysmith Black Mambazo (Showstreet Palace Theater). The first Summer Celebration included DRUMLine Live! in Celebrity Theater, which highlights musical styles from Historically Black Colleges and Universities using video screens and special effects to enhance soul, R&B, country, and other music. Renovations included upgrades to Aunt Granny's and rebranding and renaming of two shops. Work began in October 2017 on "Wildwood Grove," adding eleven new experiences, including a suspended family coaster (Dragonflier), a restaurant (Till & Harvest), an indoor play area (Hidden Hollow), an outdoor splash pad (Wildwood Creek), a swinging boat ride (The Great Tree Swing), and a 50 ft tall tree with a butterfly canopy (The Wildwood Tree). The $37 million, 5-acre development, described as "a land built from Dolly Parton's dreams," opened on May 10, 2019, as part of a $300 million 6-year expansion project. In October 2019, Dollywood announced its first new festival in 14 years, Dollywood's Flower & Food Festival, featuring 10 to 15 foot tall topiaries based on Dolly's songs like "Coat of Many Colors," photo opportunities, a rainbow sky over Showstreet, and food. The festival was originally scheduled for May 8 to June 14, 2020, but was deferred to May 7 to June 13, 2021. In October 2019, Dollywood filed plans for a new resort adjacent to Splash Country and DreamMore Resort, featuring a 310-room hotel, a 325-seat restaurant, and a conference space, creating 100 jobs. In June 2021, Dollywood announced a $500 million expansion, including details about the HeartSong Lodge & Resort, which will have 302 rooms, five floors of suites, a four-story atrium with a large central fireplace, and multiple shopping and culinary experiences. HeartSong Lodge is scheduled to open in 2023, along with campgrounds, three additional resorts, and a "record-breaking" attraction. During the 2022 off-season, the Silver Dollar Mine tunnel connecting the lower section of Craftsman's Valley and The Village was removed, creating more open space for guests to walk through and enjoy views of the Dollywood Express. The parking complex was renovated to better utilize lots at both Dollywood and Splash Country, with guest traffic lanes swapped for tram lanes, eliminating previous intersections and introducing a one-way circuit that removes the old two-way traffic pattern. Two extra parking toll booths (four attendants) and additional staging lanes were added to reduce wait times. Other improvements included renovations to Iron Horse Pizza (formerly Victoria's Pizza) for greater production capacity and seating, a complete makeover of the Emporium for a modern shopping experience, and the removal of two buildings—the former Eagle Shop and the former Christmas Cottage—to provide wider walkways. On August 5, 2022, it was announced that Big Bear Mountain, a new roller coaster under construction, opened on May 12, 2023, and is the longest in the park's history. In 2019, Dollywood won Golden Ticket awards for Best Kids' Area, Best Guest Experience, and Best Christmas Event of 2018. In 2019, Coaster101.com named Lightning Rod "Wooden Roller Coaster of the Decade." In 2021, Dollywood's Smoky Mountain Christmas won the Golden Ticket Award for Best Christmas Event for the 13th straight year. In June 2022, Tripadvisor named Dollywood the number one theme park in the U.S. Dollywood received the Applause Award in 2010 from Liseberg in Gothenburg, Sweden, recognizing its management, operations, and creative accomplishments. In 2017, Dollywood won Golden Ticket awards for Friendliest Park, Best Christmas Event, Best Food, and Best Show. In 2018, Dollywood received a Golden Ticket award in the Best Food category, marking its fourth win in seven years, and also won Golden Tickets for Best Shows, Friendliest Park, and Best Christmas Event, and was ranked third best park in the world. In the 2018 USA Today 10Best Readers' Choice Awards, Dollywood was ranked sixth best amusement park in the U.S., DreamMore Resort and Spa was ranked first in Best Amusement Park Hotel, and Aunt Granny's Restaurant was ranked first in Best Amusement Park Restaurant. Dreamland Drive-In was ranked third in Best Amusement Park Entertainment, and Dollywood's Splash Country was ranked sixth in Best Outdoor Water Park.
